note: Offline fixture for the issue bridge. Synthetic issues used to prove the deterministic classification and the rendered brief without touching GitHub. Numbers are deliberately high (9xx) so a fixture run can never collide with a real sample-service issue in a task's idempotency key. The bridge refuses --apply for a fixture source.

issues.title: Renderer drops the last frame of a multi-shot assembly
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Assemble a 3-shot timeline with a 4.2 s last shot.
2. Run the renderer with default settings.

### Expected
All frames of the last shot are present.

### Acceptance
- The assembled file contains the final frame of every shot.
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/render/...` covers the boundary case.

### Actual
The final ~0.4 s of the last shot is missing; the timeline ends early.

issues.title: Add H.265 export profile
issues.body:
### Motivation
Exporting H.265 halves the storage cost for archived renders.

### Acceptance criteria
- A `h265` profile is selectable in the export config.
- Exports round-trip: decode of the produced file matches the source resolution and frame count.
- Existing profiles are unchanged.

issues.title: Renderer crashes on unrelated flaky test
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce
Run the suite twice; a test fails once.

### Acceptance
- Isolated failure is not a renderer defect; closed with the run log attached to prove flakiness rather than a code path.

issues.title: Export dialog shows the wrong duration for a 60 s clip
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Open the export dialog for a 60 s clip.
2. Read the duration shown next to the profile selector.

### Expected
The dialog shows 60 s (00:01:00).

### Acceptance
- The dialog shows the clip's real duration for 60 s and 3 600 s clips.
- A screenshot of both states is attached to the issue before it is closed.

### Actual
It shows 00:00:60.

### Filed by
qa role, visual check of the export dialog (screenshot attached to the PR).
